concepts.proposed_markdown: Metronome documents three discount patterns for committed usage: reduce a prepaid commit's cost basis, apply commit-specific contract overrides, or select reusable commit rates defined on a rate card. Cost-basis discounts are limited to prepaid commits with a uniform percentage reduction and do not change usage-statement prices. Commit-specific overwrite overrides take priority over commit-specific multipliers, followed by contract-level overwrites and contract-level multipliers; narrower commit association does not itself win priority.
warnings: Keep cost-basis discounting limited to prepaid commits; the guide says postpaid invoice and access amounts must match.
The guide lists tiered commit-specific overrides but its displayed precedence sequence explicitly enumerates only overwrite and multiplier overrides.
The cost-basis example payload appears one order of magnitude below its stated $10,000 access and $8,000 invoice amounts under documented USD-cent scaling.

concepts.proposed_markdown: - [[source-metronome-guides-pricing-packaging-apply-credits-and-commits-discounting-on-commits]] — prepaid cost-basis discounts, commit-specific override scope and precedence, and commit-rate selection

Rate-card commit rates are supported only for usage products. A commit rate must be added together with a list rate in the same pricing unit; both can be tiered, and tier quantity does not reset when consumption moves between commit and list rates. If a commit or credit selects commit-rate behavior for a product without a configured commit rate, Metronome applies the list rate and list-rate overrides while ignoring commit-rate overrides.
warnings: Do not infer rounding, effective-date overlap, retroactive invoice recalculation, or finalized-invoice behavior from this guide.
The fallback is product-specific: preserve the condition that the given product lacks a commit rate.
